name: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company
blurb: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is a global enterprise technology company spun off from Hewlett-Packard in 2015, tracing its corporate lineage to 1939. It operates across five segments — Server, Hybrid Cloud, Networking, Financial Services, and Corporate Investments — selling products such as HPE ProLiant servers, HPE Cray EX supercomputers, HPE Synergy composable infrastructure, and HPE Edgeline edge systems. With trailing-twelve-month revenue of approximately $35.7 billion and 67,000+ employees worldwide, HPE serves enterprise and government customers across the Americas, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific. Its strategic focus has shifted toward AI-optimized servers and hybrid cloud solutions as demand for high-performance computing accelerates.
recent: HPE shares surged 6.16% to $32.07 on May 13, 2026 — touching the top of its 52-week range ($17.03–$32.53) — and continued rising pre-market on May 14; the specific catalyst was not disclosed in available sources. The stock's market cap has expanded roughly 96% over the trailing period, reflecting strong investor appetite for its AI server exposure. Next earnings are scheduled for June 1, 2026, with analysts holding a consensus Buy but a price target of $26.82, below the current trading level.
